seed: Switching a shape's border off should leave the row behind on the next shape, switched off, holding the numbers it had. Reported on 2026-09-08: turn the border off on a box and draw another box, and the new box has no Border row at all, so the only way back to a line is the plus, which hands you a standard one at the standard width on the outside. Every other effect behaves the opposite way: switch a shadow off, draw another shape, and the shadow row is still there, switched off, with all its numbers, so one click brings it back exactly as it was. This walk tunes a border to something distinctive, switches it off, draws another box, and holds that box to carrying the same row: off, still Outside, still the width it was set to, painting nothing, and one press away from the line it had.

steps.note: a box whose border has been made distinctive: thicker than the one it arrived with, and drawn outside its edge rather than inside, where a border starts.

the same box with the border switched off rather than removed. The line is gone from the canvas and the row is still in the list, holding its width and its Outside, which is what a switch means everywhere else in this panel.

THE CLAIM: the box drawn after the border was switched off carries a Border row of its own, switched off, still Outside, still at the width the last one was set to. It paints no line, which is what the user asked for on 2026-09-06, and it is one press from the line it had rather than a trip to the plus.
one press on that row and the line is back, and it is the line the first box had: the same width, drawn outside the edge, not a standard new one at the standard width.
an oval beside them, untouched by anything done to a rectangle: its own border is on and inside, where a shape's line starts.

removing the row with the cross still means gone for good: the box after it has no Border row at all. That is the difference the switch is for, and it is why keeping the row on a switch-off does not take anything away.
